name: Old Quarter
dotReason: Worth a special trip in this corridor
summary: Sleep here when the walk is the reason: tube houses, shopfronts, and the street north of Hoan Kiem Lake. Vietnam Tourism calls the Old Quarter one square kilometre of 36 streets, and admission to the lanes is free. Sleep elsewhere in Hanoi when a citadel morning is the trip.
getThere: Walk north from Hoan Kiem Lake
bestMonths: April to June, or September to December
seoTitle: Old Quarter walk — tube houses, Bach Ma, Dong Xuan
seoDescription: Walk Hanoi’s Old Quarter, one square kilometre of 36 streets north of Hoan Kiem Lake. The lanes are free. Bach Ma and Dong Xuan sit on the same walk.
intro: The lanes are narrow-front houses that run deep, with courtyards cut in for light. Vietnam Tourism calls those tube houses. Shop streets still use the old trade names. The Ha Noi page dates the grid to the 14th century. The attractions page dates it to the 15th century.

Walk them from the lake. The same office prints the quarter as free to enter, and open from 7am to midnight. Morning is the easier hour on the pavement. Bach Ma is the temple at 76 Hang Buom. Dong Xuan is the covered market at the north end.
Pho and bun cha are the bowls named for these lanes, and egg coffee is the cup. The Hanoi food guide is the menu. Stall prices: check on arrival.
gettingAround: Walk north from Hoan Kiem Lake. Dan Tri prints about 2 km from the lake to Dong Xuan. Travel.com.vn prints about 800 m. Minutes: check on arrival. Vietnam Tourism suggests a cyclo for a first look, then the streets on foot.

stayAreas.name: Near Hoan Kiem
stayAreas.summary: Travel.com.vn names the lake side when you want the market and the center on one walk. Hang Dao is the street that runs north from that end.

stayAreas.name: Hang Buom and Ma May
stayAreas.summary: Travel.com.vn names Hang Buom, Ma May, and Hang Be when the walk to Dong Xuan is the point. The evening corner Vietnam Tourism names is Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen.

eat: Pho and bun cha are the bowls Vietnam Tourism names in these lanes, and egg coffee is the cup. The Hanoi food guide is the menu. Stall prices: check on arrival.
interestsBody: Dining is pho, bun cha, and egg coffee in the lanes. The Hanoi food guide is the menu.
Shopping is Dong Xuan, then the trade streets Vietnam Tourism still names: Hang Bac for silver, Hang Gai for silk, Hang Ma for festival goods, and Lan Ong for herbs.
The walk is the lanes themselves. Bach Ma is the temple on Hang Buom. At night, Vietnam Tourism points to the corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen. No drink price is printed there.

blocks.heading: Dong Xuan Market
paragraphs: Dong Xuan is the covered market at the north end, on Dong Xuan street. Travel.com.vn puts the management office at 1A Cau Dong. Dan Tri describes three floors, with clothes and accessories on the ground floor and a dry-goods area called Bac Qua.

Dan Tri prints 06:00–18:00 every day, and 22:30 on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. Travel.com.vn says stall hours can change and to check before you go, and that there is no entry ticket. Dan Tri does not print a fee. Confirm both at the door.
Hang Bac still sells silver, Hang Gai sells silk, Hang Ma sells festival goods, and Lan Ong sells herbs. Vietnam Tourism names those streets. No single shop is listed here.

cards.title: Dong Xuan Market
cards.summary: Bolts of cloth in the hall. Dan Tri and Travel.com.vn do not print the same hours, and only one of them prints an entry rule.

interestGroups.title: Walking the lanes
interestGroups.summary: Walk the tube-house streets from the lake. Bach Ma is the temple on the way.

cards.title: Bach Ma Temple
cards.summary: The temple at 76 Hang Buom. The 2025 ticket is 20,000 VND. The printed hours do not match.

blocks.heading: The streets
paragraphs: Vietnam Tourism calls the quarter one square kilometre of 36 streets, north of Hoan Kiem Lake, free to enter, and open from 7am to midnight. The Ha Noi page dates the lanes to the 14th century. The attractions page dates them to the 15th century.
Tube houses are the narrow fronts that run deep, with courtyards for light. A cyclo is the first look the tourism page suggests. After that, walk.
Bach Ma is at 76 Hang Buom. At night, Vietnam Tourism points to the corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen. No drink price is printed there.

faqs.q: Is there a ticket for the lanes?
faqs.a: Vietnam Tourism prints admission as free, and hours from 7am to midnight. Bach Ma is a separate ticket of 20,000 VND from 8 December 2025. For Dong Xuan, Travel.com.vn says there is no entry ticket and Dan Tri does not print a fee, so confirm at the door.
Vietnam Tourism’s climate page names April to June, and September to December, for Ha Noi. The Ha Noi page also prints September to November. June to August is the rainy stretch.

faqs.q: Which Bach Ma hours do I trust?
faqs.a: The 2025 notice prints 08:00–12:00 and 13:30–17:30, with a Friday-to-Sunday evening that closes at 21:30 in that notice and at 21:00 in VnExpress. A 2018 door board prints 08:00–11:00 and 14:00–17:00, Monday closed, and 08:00–21:00 on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month. Read the board at the gate.

season.label: Clearer walking months
season.note: Vietnam Tourism’s climate page names April to June, and September to December, for Ha Noi. The Ha Noi page also prints September to November. June to August is the rainy stretch. The lanes are walked in all of these.
